title: I have no sound
summary: Covers muted devices, wrong output selection, disabled enhancements, driver problems and faulty audio hardware.

scope.question: Is there no sound at all, or does it work sometimes?
scope.help: Complete silence points to output selection or drivers; intermittent sound often means a loose jack or a physical fault.

options.label: Completely silent everywhere
Sound works sometimes, or cuts out
Sound works but quality is bad, distorted or crackly
Sound works on headphones but not speakers, or the reverse

output_device.question: In Windows sound settings, which device is set as the output?
output_device.help: Windows often switches output automatically when you plug in headphones and forgets to switch back.

options.label: It is set to my speakers or headphones
It is set to something else, such as a monitor or HDMI output
There are no output devices listed at all
I cannot find the sound settings

open_sound_settings.question: Open Sound settings with the Windows key plus I, then Control Panel. What do you see under Output?
open_sound_settings.help: Win plus I opens Settings. Then choose System > Sound.

options.label: My output device is listed there
No output device is listed

volume_state.question: Is the volume slider at zero, and is the selected device muted?
volume_state.help: Per-application volume and exclusive mode can also silence a device while the main slider is high.

options.label: It was muted or at zero
The volume is high and not muted
I checked and it is unmuted and high

enhancements.question: Are audio enhancements or spatial sound enabled on the device?
enhancements.help: Enhancements, spatial sound and exclusive mode apps all cause silence on otherwise working hardware.

options.label: Yes, enhancements or spatial sound are on
No, they are off
I have not checked

app_test.question: Do you hear sound from Windows test sounds, such as the sample in sound settings?
app_test.help: The Test button plays a sound through the selected device, which tells you whether Windows or the device is at fault.

options.label: Yes, the test sound plays
No, the test sound is also silent
Only some apps are silent

device_present.question: Does the audio device appear in Device Manager under Sound, video and game controllers?
device_present.help: A missing or disabled device is a driver or hardware problem rather than a settings one.

options.label: It shows a yellow exclamation mark
It is greyed out
It is not listed at all
It is there and looks normal

intermittent.question: Does it cut out in a regular pattern, or completely at random?
intermittent.help: Regular patterns usually mean interference or a driver bug; random cutouts usually mean a physical connection or hardware fault.

options.label: Regularly, such as every few minutes
Completely at random
Only when I move the laptop or cable

loose_connection.question: Is this a laptop or do you use external speakers or a headset?
loose_connection.help: Headphone jacks and ports get worn, and internal laptop speakers rely on small connectors that can work loose.

options.label: I use headphones, earbuds or external speakers with a cable
It is a laptop with built-in speakers
Desktop speakers plugged into a rear port

audio_quality.question: Is the problem crackling, distortion, low volume, or a delay compared with the video?
audio_quality.help: Each symptom points at something different, from sample rate mismatch to a failing speaker.

options.label: Crackling, popping or distortion
Audio is out of sync with video
It is just very quiet

headphone_speaker_test.question: If you plug headphones into the same port that the speakers used, do they work?
headphone_speaker_test.help: This isolates whether the port works at all and whether the fault is the speaker or the audio path.

options.label: Headphones work in that port
Headphones are silent too
Headphones and speakers use different ports

result_wrong_output.title: Select the right output device
result_wrong_output.diagnosis: Connecting a monitor or TV over HDMI makes it the default output, which leaves speakers silent without any error.
steps: Press Win plus I and go to System > Sound > Output
Choose your speakers or headphones from the device list
Test with the Test button to confirm sound
Also check the volume mixer: Win plus I > Sound > Volume mixer, and confirm the right device is not muted
For Bluetooth, pair the device again in Bluetooth settings and set it as the output
To stop Windows switching automatically, open Device Manager, open the output device's Properties, and untick Allow applications to take exclusive control of this device

result_volume_fixed.title: Volume and mute settings
result_volume_fixed.diagnosis: Muted outputs and per-application volume sliders explain a surprising number of 'no sound' reports.
steps: Check the main volume slider in Settings > System > Sound and drag it up
Check the device is not muted by clicking the speaker icon in the taskbar
Open the volume mixer and check each application, since browsers have their own sliders
Check the device's own physical volume buttons or knob, if it has one
Run the Test button in sound settings to confirm the device produces sound at all
If you use Bluetooth, check the device's own volume, since some headsets have a separate Bluetooth volume

result_disable_enhancements.title: Turn off enhancements and spatial sound
result_disable_enhancements.diagnosis: Audio enhancements, spatial sound and mono audio are designed features that can silence a working device.
steps: Open Settings > System > Sound, then click on your output device and Device properties
Open the Enhancements tab and tick Disable all enhancements, or untick each individual enhancement
Turn spatial sound off, or try the Windows Sonic option instead of the hardware setting
In Device properties > Advanced, untick Allow applications to take exclusive control of this device
Turn off Mono audio, which is often left on after accessibility adjustments
Restart Windows and test again
warnings: Mono audio makes everything play through one channel. If it seems stuck on, check Settings > Accessibility > Audio.

result_per_app_volume.title: Check per-application and exclusive mode settings
result_per_app_volume.diagnosis: If Windows test sounds work but your applications are silent, the problem is per-app volume or exclusive mode control.
steps: Open the volume mixer and raise the level for the affected application, and unmute it
Click the Properties button for that application and untick Mute for its output device
In Device Manager, open your audio device's Properties > Advanced and untick Allow applications to take exclusive control
Restart the affected application, since some only read audio settings at launch
Check the browser's own audio settings, since browsers mute tabs separately
Test with a different application to narrow down whether it is one app or all of them
warnings: Some professional audio software needs exclusive mode. If you use it, re-enable exclusive control afterwards.

result_audio_driver.title: Clean reinstall the audio driver
result_audio_driver.diagnosis: A corrupt Realtek audio driver is one of the most common causes of Windows silence.
steps: Open Device Manager and expand Sound, video and game controllers
Right-click the audio device and choose Uninstall device, ticking Delete the driver software
Restart and let Windows install a basic driver so sound works again
Then install the official driver from your PC vendor, or download the Realtek driver from our driver section
Update the chipset driver as well, since the audio driver depends on it
If you have an onboard HDMI audio device, make sure it is not set as the output instead
warnings: After removing the driver you may have no sound until Windows reinstalls it. Have the installer downloaded beforehand.
Do not use third-party driver updater software, which commonly installs unsigned or mismatched drivers.

result_device_manager_code.title: Read the Device Manager code
result_device_manager_code.diagnosis: Device Manager gives a specific code, and each one has a defined fix.
steps: Open Device Manager and expand Sound, video and game controllers
Double-click the device with the yellow exclamation mark
Read the code on the General tab, such as Code 10, 28, 43 or 31
Look it up in our Device Manager error guide for the exact fix
Code 28 means no driver at all, so install from your PC vendor
Use Scan for hardware changes from the Action menu if you have just connected audio hardware

result_enable_device.title: Enable the audio device
result_enable_device.diagnosis: A greyed-out device in Device Manager is simply disabled and needs enabling rather than any repair.
steps: Right-click the greyed-out device and choose Enable device
If the option is missing, choose Uninstall device, restart, and let Windows reinstall it
Check hidden devices with View > Show hidden devices, since disabled devices appear greyed out there
On a laptop, confirm the audio device is not disabled by a function key
Restart after enabling, since the driver loads at startup

result_missing_device.title: The audio hardware is not detected
result_missing_device.diagnosis: A completely missing audio device points to hardware, BIOS or firmware rather than drivers.
steps: Enter BIOS with Del or F2 and check whether an onboard audio device is listed and enabled
Some BIOS settings disable onboard audio when a discrete sound card is detected
In BIOS, load defaults in case the audio setting was changed
Update BIOS firmware, since older firmware can fail to detect newer audio chips
If a USB audio interface or headset is used, try a different port, preferably a rear motherboard port
If the device is still missing, the onboard audio chip or its connection has failed and needs hardware repair
warnings: On a laptop, the internal speaker connector or codec can fail. That is a repair, not a driver fix.

result_plug_and_jack.title: Check the plug and the jack
result_plug_and_jack.diagnosis: Worn headphone jacks and cables cause sound that cuts out when the cable moves slightly.
steps: Push the plug fully in until it clicks, and wiggle it gently at the jack to see whether sound cuts out
Try a different pair of headphones or earbuds to rule out the cable
Check the jack for lint or debris, and clean it gently with a soft brush or compressed air
Move to the next jack if the device has several, since some are disabled for headphone detect
Avoid hanging the cable by its plug, which is the most common cause of jack failure
Replace a cable that cuts out when moved; internal headphone wiring breaks at the connector
warnings: Do not use metal objects to clean a jack; you can short the contacts and damage the audio chip.
Do not hang headphones from the plug or yank the cable out, both of which destroy the connector.

result_internal_speakers.title: Test the laptop's internal speakers
result_internal_speakers.diagnosis: A laptop that loses sound when moved usually has a loose internal speaker connector.
steps: Check the volume mixer to confirm the speakers are not muted for the laptop's own output
Run the Windows test sound with the lid open, since some laptops mute when closed
Test with headphones; if they work, the speakers or their connector are at fault
Move the laptop gently and listen for cutting, which indicates a loose internal connector
Open the laptop and reseat the speaker connector, only if you are comfortable doing so
Otherwise a repair centre can reseat it cheaply and it is a common laptop repair
warnings: Opening a laptop risks damaging ribbon cables and the battery connector. Disconnect the battery first if you do.
Some laptops mute when the lid is closed by design, which is not a fault.

result_rear_port.title: Try the other rear ports
result_rear_port.diagnosis: Desktop speakers on the wrong rear port, or in the speaker-out port instead of line-out, are extremely common mistakes.
steps: Plug the speakers into the green line-out port, not the pink microphone port or the black rear speaker port
On a desktop with a graphics card with its own audio outputs, use the ports on the card rather than the motherboard
If sound plays on the wrong port, choose that port as the output in sound settings, or change the cable
Try a different rear port to rule out a faulty one
Check the speaker power LED and that the volume knob on the speakers is turned up
Confirm the correct output is selected in Settings > System > Sound > Output
warnings: Connecting microphones or line-in to speakers can produce very loud noise or damage the microphone. Check the colour coding.

result_speaker_problem.title: The speakers themselves are faulty
result_speaker_problem.diagnosis: Headphones working in the same port proves the audio path is fine, so the speakers or their power are at fault.
steps: Check the speaker power LED is on and the volume knob is turned up
Confirm the correct input on the speakers, which is often a source selector button
Swap the left and right cables at the back, since speakers with two inputs need the correct one
Test the speakers with a phone or another device to confirm they work at all
Replace any power supply brick that feels warm, buzzes or smells burnt
Check for a blown driver by playing something with heavy bass, since small drivers do not handle low frequencies well
warnings: Disconnect the speakers from the PC before testing them with another device, to rule out the PC as the source of damage.
Do not leave a buzzing power supply connected, and never open it.

result_sample_rate.title: Fix crackling and distortion
result_sample_rate.diagnosis: Crackling usually comes from a sample rate mismatch or exclusive mode contention rather than broken hardware.
steps: Open Settings > System > Sound > your output device > Device properties > Advanced
Untick Allow applications to take exclusive control of this device
Set the default format to 16 bit, 44100 Hz, which is the most compatible setting
Change the format to 24 bit, 48000 Hz if you handle video or music production, and test for crackling
Test with all audio enhancements off
If using Bluetooth, connect with the higher-quality codec option available in the device properties
warnings: Do not set an unusual sample rate if you are not sure your hardware supports it. Wrong rates cause crackling or silence.

result_bluetooth_latency.title: Reduce Bluetooth audio delay
result_bluetooth_latency.diagnosis: Bluetooth audio always has some delay. Large delays usually mean the wrong codec is being used.
steps: In Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Devices, open your headset's properties
Choose the high-quality audio codec option, such as aptX or AAC, instead of the legacy SBC codec
Switch between the available codecs and test the delay for each
Update the headset's firmware if the manufacturer provides an app for it
Reduce the distance and remove obstructions between the PC and the headset
Switch to 2.4 GHz with a dongle if you need near-zero latency for video or gaming
warnings: Bluetooth audio codecs are licensed, so options vary by headset and Windows version.
Switching to 2.4 GHz uses more USB bandwidth and can conflict with other 2.4 GHz devices.

result_quiet_audio.title: Fix quiet audio
result_quiet_audio.diagnosis: Several separate volume controls multiply together, and any one of them set low will cause quiet output.
steps: Raise the main volume slider in Settings > System > Sound
Raise the level for the specific application in the volume mixer
Turn up the volume on the speaker or headset itself
Check Windows Loudness Equalization in Sound properties > Enhancements, which can make quiet sources audible
Check per-app volume settings in Settings > System > Sound > Volume mixer for a separate control
Update the audio driver, since some versions scale volume incorrectly
warnings: Loudness Equalization is a software boost, so raising it can sound harsh or introduce distortion at high levels.

result_driver_interference.title: Find the interference
result_driver_interference.diagnosis: Regularly repeating cutouts usually mean a driver conflict or an audio enhancement process competing for the device.
steps: Uninstall audio enhancements and disable spatial sound in the output device properties
Turn off exclusive mode control for the audio device
Close communication apps such as Discord, Teams and Zoom, which hook the microphone and speaker
Uninstall or disable third-party virtual audio drivers, such as those from screen recorders or voice changers
Update the Realtek audio driver and chipset drivers from your PC vendor
Check whether the pattern follows a specific app by testing playback in the Windows Media Player
warnings: If you rely on a virtual audio device for recording, remove competing virtual audio software rather than removing your recording tool.
